summary: Customer wants an optical measurement during yeast fermentation to follow growth and detect changes earlier. Biomass and metabolic signals are mentioned but not defined as separate targets. Broth becomes more optically dense during the run. They request help setting up an initial feasibility study with reference measurements.

facts_stated.text: An optical measurement is wanted during yeast fermentation.
Purpose is to follow growth and detect changes earlier.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: follow growth and notice changes earlier

facts_stated.text: The broth becomes more optically dense over the run.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The broth becomes more optically dense as the run develops

physical_state.enquiry_quote: The broth becomes more optically dense as the run develops

customer_premises.claim: Biomass and metabolic signals are treated as a single combined request rather than defined targets
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: both a biomass signal and a metabolic signal, but these have not been defined as separate targets

customer_premises.claim: They assume an optical measurement will be feasible and useful for their fermentation without prior evidence
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: We would like an optical measurement during yeast fermentation

customer_premises.claim: They assume a feasibility study with reference measurements can be set up as the next step
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: We need help turning this request into an initial feasibility study with useful reference measurements

unknowns: Definition of the biomass target (e.g. cell density range, units, reference method such as offline OD or dry weight)
Definition of the metabolic signal (which metabolites, e.g. glucose, ethanol, and their concentration ranges)
Matrix composition and interferences (medium components, pH, dissolved CO2, bubbles)
Temperature and pressure of the fermentation
Installation point (in-line probe, bypass, at-line) and optical access
Distance between measurement point and analyser
Required accuracy, detection limits and response time
Reference measurement availability and sampling frequency for the feasibility study
Scale and type of fermenter (lab, pilot, production)
Whether the optical density change is due to biomass alone or other turbidity sources
